text:
maya: Heads-up — running into a weird TS inference/overload regression when using the SDK from an Edge worker bundle. Behavior differs between ESM build (Vite) and CJS transpiled build (webpack).

maya: Repro: simple client `request` overloads where we have `request<T>(opts: RequestOpts<T>): Promise<Response<T>>` vs `request(opts: RequestOpts): Promise<Response>` — in ESM the generic is inferred, in CJS it falls back to `unknown` and forces callers to cast.

maya: Minimal example:
```ts
// sdk.ts
export function request<T>(opts: { body?: T }): Promise<{ data?: T }>;
export function request(opts: any) { return fetch('/').then(r => r.json()); }
```

maya: In a Vite edge bundle: `const r = await request({body:{x:1}})` -> `r.data.x` types ok. In our webpack legacy CJS build used by some customers (and SSRed edge transform) `r.data` becomes `unknown`.

maya: Also noticed this correlates with `tsconfig.module` + `compilerOptions.declaration` + `esModuleInterop` combos. Changing `skipLibCheck` helps locally but customers hit this without that flag.

sam: ugh. Is it definitely the overload resolution step or something in our distributed .d.ts shape?

sam: can you paste the built .d.ts (both ESM and CJS package entrypoints) — maybe we accidentally emit a non-generic overload first in one build which makes inference fail.

maya: will paste shortly. I think webpack build ends up with `export =` style or a `module.exports =` transform for the runtime, which affects how TS picks the signature when consuming via `import sdk from 'redwood-sdk'` vs `import * as sdk`.

ken: runtime note: Edge runtimes (Cloudflare/Workers) often run code through different bundlers/plugins that rewrite default/named exports. If consuming code does `const sdk = require('redwood-sdk')` that can change the TS resolution if `.d.ts` uses `export default`.

lia: On the typing side, overload ordering / variance matters. TS picks the first overload that matches; if our declaration file emits a broad `request(opts: any): Promise<any>` before the generic overload it will shadow it. I bet ESM build emits the generic-first entrypoint, CJS emits a fallback-first.

maya: exact — ESM index.d.ts snippet:
```ts
export declare function request<T>(opts: RequestOpts<T>): Promise<Response<T>>;
export declare function request(opts: RequestOpts): Promise<Response>;
```

maya: CJS index.d.ts snippet:
```ts
export declare function request(opts: RequestOpts): Promise<Response>;
export declare function request<T>(opts: RequestOpts<T>): Promise<Response<T>>;
```

maya: so inference breaks. Not sure whether the ordering is from our rollup plugin or from typedoc generation pipeline.

sam: quick fix: ensure our dts bundler (dts-rollup / tsup) preserves overload order (generic-first). We should add a test that consumes the built package with TS 4.9/5.x and verifies inference on a small snippet.

ken: For edge compatibility, also ensure consumers using `@edge-runtime` toolchains don't rely on `esModuleInterop` hacks. Recommend we publish both `exports` map entries: `import` (ESM) and `require` (CJS) and make sure both reference the same single .d.ts file (not duplicated). Duplicate triples often cause different declaration emit ordering.

lia: Another angle: `unknown` vs `any` — the CJS fallback ends up typed as `any` at runtime but TS shows `unknown` because of stricter lib settings in some consumer tsconfigs. We should avoid `unknown` in public surface unless intentional. Maybe change fallback overload to `any` to be pragmatic while we fix ordering. 

sam: meh I'd rather fix ordering; changing public surface to use `any` is a breaking-compat/quality regression. But ok as temporary mitigation behind a patch release.

maya: Auth/retry interactions: also found that our `Client` generic overloads (Client<Auth,Opts>) lose their generics when used with `createClient()` wrapper in certain bundlers because the wrapper is emitted as `export =` in the CJS build. That causes consumers to get `Client<any, any>`. Hit a few customer bug reports about auth middleware typings disappearing.

ken: We should audit `createClient` export shape. If wrapper is `module.exports = createClient` then TS consumers using `import { createClient } from 'redwood-sdk'` get different resolution semantics. Exports map + `types` link can help.

lia: Proposed action items:
- Add CI test that installs the built tarball via both `npm pack` and `yarn pack` and runs `tsc --noEmit` against a small consumer project (ESM and CJS scenarios).
- Canonicalize dts generation: single source .d.ts produced once, referenced by both `exports` entrypoints, ensure overload order preserved.
- Add a short doc in SDK migration notes: recommended `tsconfig` options for consumers (moduleResolution, esModuleInterop, skipLibCheck caveats).
- Short-term patch: reorder overloads or adjust fallback typed to be generic-friendly.

maya: I'll open a PR with a failing CI consumer test and pair with you sam to adjust the bundler.

sam: sg. Also add a lint rule to our declared types (dtslint-ish) to catch fallback-first overloads. Maybe we can run a small AST check post-dts bundle that flags a non-generic overload before a generic one for the same symbol.

ken: When shipping fix, include a note for Dedicated/Private customers: if you self-host older CJS packaged SDKs, you'll want to update to avoid losing type inference in adapter layers.

lia: FYI deploy-bot: new thread created for tracking — please create issue if CI test fails.

deploy-bot: Created issue #4227 in devex/typing "ts inference mismatch between ESM/CJS builds" and attached failing consumer test artifacts. :white_check_mark:

maya: thanks — I'll drop the PR link in this thread once ready. TL;DR: ordering of overloads in emitted .d.ts is the prime suspect; CI consumer test + single .d.ts export should fix.

sam: thanks all. small follow-ups only, I can pick up the bundler change after your PR lands.
